fdroid:com.reteget.name: ReteGet
fdroid:com.reteget.summary: File and APK downloader with its own TLS 1.3, for Android 2.3 and newer
fdroid:com.reteget.description:
ReteGet downloads files and APKs straight onto old Android phones and tablets — Android 2.3 and newer — without a computer, ADB or an app store.
Old phones are cut off from most of the web. Android 2.3 has no TLS 1.2 at all, and Android 4.1 devices such as the Galaxy Note 2 fail against modern servers with "SSLv3 alert handshake failure". So ReteGet carries its own TLS client, written in plain Java: TLS 1.3 (X25519 or P-256, AES-128-GCM, ECDSA and RSA-PSS server signatures), and TLS 1.2 only for servers without TLS 1.3, with downgrade protection. Because Android 2.3 cannot verify ECDSA certificates such as GitHub's, the app also parses X.509 certificates and validates the chain itself, against the system and the bundled root certificates, and always checks the host name. The system TLS is tried first; the built-in engine takes over when it fails, or always, if you tick the option.
Features
* Download queue at the top of the screen: one download at a time, with the file name, state, URL and a progress bar for each entry. Failed downloads say why and can be retried; finished APKs can be installed from the list. Select all / Delete selected. The list survives closing the app.
* URL templates: a URL such as .../download/v{1}/app-{1}.apk shows a small field for {1}, so an update is just a new version number.
* Presets with names, including the rete series (ReteGet, ReteClock, ReteKey) with their expected checksums and signing keys filled in. Use, Edit, Up, Dn and Del on each preset.
* Latest: a preset can name an index page (a directory listing, or GitHub's releases API); Latest downloads the newest file there that fits the preset URL, in Windows Explorer order (0.3.10 after 0.3.9). The rete presets come with it.
* Checksum check: SHA-256, SHA-1, MD5 and SHA-512, pasted as a bare hash or a sha256sum line.
* APK signing-key check: warns when an APK is signed by a different key than the installed app or the last download of it.
* Installs APKs with the system installer; for an upgrade with the same signing key and a newer version it opens the installer right away, and you confirm there.
* HTTP, HTTPS, passive FTP, FTPS (ftpes://, ftps://) and SFTP.
* FTPS with its own TLS, reusing the TLS session on the data connection as servers require; a self-signed certificate is confirmed by fingerprint once and then pinned.
* SFTP with its own SSH-2 client (works on Android 2.3): the server's host key fingerprint is confirmed on first use and a changed key is refused; log in with a password or with a key generated on the phone or imported from OpenSSH (Ed25519, RSA), chosen per address or preset. Keys with a passphrase stay encrypted on the phone.
* Browse server folders over SFTP, FTP, FTPS and http(s) (WebDAV or an index page): check files and folders and download them, folders with their subfolders.
* An https download that the server redirects to plain http stops and asks first.
* Broken HTTP downloads continue where they stopped (Range with If-Range): automatically up to three times, and with Retry, also after the app was closed.
* Password-protected servers: http://user:password@host/path, answered with Digest (SHA-256, MD5) or Basic only when the server asks, and only to that address. Passwords are shown as *** and left out of settings exports.
* Settings export and import (presets, options, signing keys) as a plain text file in the subset of INI and TOML that both read the same way, or through the clipboard.
* Saves to the system Download folder; when shared storage is unavailable, to the app's own storage, from where APKs can still be installed.
* Paste and Clear buttons for the URL and the checksum.
Small and self-contained: plain Java and the Android framework, no third-party libraries, a single dex file, built without Gradle.
The option to allow unverified certificates exists for home servers with self-signed certificates; leave it off otherwise.

PRICING

fdroid:io.github.RealEarthling.epoch.name: Epoch
fdroid:io.github.RealEarthling.epoch.summary: Time display for nerds: Unix, sidereal, binary clocks & more.
fdroid:io.github.RealEarthling.epoch.description:
Epoch shows the current moment across a wide range of time systems — updating every second, all in one place. 31 values, from Unix time and sidereal time to Swatch Internet Time and the Doomsday Clock.
 What Epoch gives you 
- Civil: date, time, day second, day minute, day percent, seven-segment clock, analog clock with 12 or 24-hour face — for any time zone
- Technical: Unix time, International Atomic Time (TAI), GPS time
- Astronomical: Greenwich and Local Mean Sidereal Time (GMST, LMST), Julian Date and six variants
- Curiosities: decimal time, Swatch Internet Time, New Earth Time, Doomsday Clock, Roman numerals time, 3 binary clocks, octal and hexadecimal time
Copy any value to clipboard with one tap or long press.
 Time zones, done thoroughly 
- Every IANA time zone, found by city, country, capital, name, abbreviation or UTC offset — in English and German.
- Epoch brings its own up-to-date time zone data, so even phones that no longer get system updates show the right time and the right clock changes.
- 7-day advance notice of clock changes, with upcoming transitions in the value's info dialog.
- Optionally pin time zones to always show standard or summer time.
 Time Shift 
Show any moment between 1970 and 2038 in all time systems, running or frozen, without touching your system clock. Check past clock change rules, leap seconds or Doomsday Clock settings, or simply pause time.
 Configurable 
- Build your own Watchlist tabs — combine any value from any category, in any order.
- All built-in tabs (Civil, Technical, Astronomical, Curiosities) are fully customizable too, and can be hidden and restored anytime.
- Set custom labels, section headers, and dividers.
- Reorder by drag-and-drop, swipe to remove.
- Customize date and time formats, configure time zone information.
- Export, import, and reset all preferences.
 Focus mode 
- Double-tap any value for a full-screen, always-on display — ideal as a bedside clock.
- Adjustable brightness (Android) and text color.
- Toggle details with a long press.
- Burn-in protection through gentle, periodic pixel shifting (especially useful on OLED screens).
- Optionally start the app directly in Focus mode.
 Designed for night use 
Night mode displays red text on black — preserving your eyes' dark adaptation for stargazing.
 Example configurations and documentation 
Ready-to-import example configurations (spaceflight, world time zone explorer, ...), a config manual and the time zone search guide are available on GitHub.
 Privacy first 
No ads, notifications, tracking, analytics, or network requests.
All settings stored locally on your device.
No permissions required.
For Local Mean Sidereal Time: optionally grant location access once (coarse, no GPS) or enter longitude manually.
Free software (GPL-3.0-or-later), reproducible builds.
Available in English and German.

fdroid:org.noise_planet.noisecapture.description:
NoiseCapture App is an application dedicated to the evaluation of your noise environment . It allows to perform measurements and, thus, to give information on your noise exposure. In addition, you can contribute to the realization of collaborative (or community) noise maps by anonymously sharing your measurements.
 New ! :
If your smartphone is already calibrated, you can now calibrate other smartphones with the application, based on the ambient noise. Select Automatic Calibration in the Calibration menu, in "Transmitter" mode for the reference smartphone and "Receiver" mode for the smartphones to be calibrated. Approach the smartphones together and start calibration from the reference smartphone. The rest is automatic.
 Features :
• Noise measurement and calculation of acoustic indicators (Leq, Lamin, LAmax, LA10, LA50, LA90...) on a journey
• Measurement description (text, photo, tags)
• Viewing measurements on a map
• Measurement history
• Smartphone calibration with a reference device
• Detailed help on using the application
 Recommendations for the 'best' measurement (see Help for details):
• The smartphone should not be in the pocket but hand held
• The smartphone microphone should not be hidden
• The noise measurement must be carried out without adding noise!
• It is possible to use an external and calibrated microphone
 Contribute to collaborative noise maps :
• Allow the transfer of measures into the community
• Realize mmeasurement outside buildings
• Do not measure when rainning or with wind
• Goto the collaborative noise map : http://noise-planet.org/map_noisecapture/index.html 
 Contribute to the NoiseCapture project :
• conttribute to the code development: https://github.com/Ifsttar/NoiseCapture 
• share your comments, questions: https://github.com/Ifsttar/NoiseCapture/issues 
• organize NoiseCapture Party to map your sound environment: http://noise-planet.org/ 
------------------------------------------------------
 NoiseCapture App respects your private life : 
• You fully control how the information is sent to the server
• Only anonymous data is transferred
• There are no audio recording: only acoustic indicators are calculated and transferred
• NoiseCapture App requires only strictly necessary permissions
 Warning: 
• Although NoiseCapture App is developed by specialists, keep in mind that a smartphone will never replace a professional sound meter. If you need advanced expertise, contact a professional.
• The quality of the measurement depends on the technical performance of your smartphone and its calibration. Depending on the nature of your phone and the version of Android used, it is possible that you can not measure with sufficient accuracy.
NoiseCapture App is the result of collaboration between two French research laboratories, the Laboratory of Environmental Acoustics (Ifsttar) and DECIDE team of Lab-STICC (CNRS), with a support from the European Commission.
More information: http://noise-planet.org/

Remmina is a remote-desktop client written in GTK, to use other desktops remotely, from a tiny
 screen or large monitors.
 Remmina supports multiple network protocols in an integrated and consistent user interface.
 The protocols currently supported are: X2Go, RDP (Remote Desktop Protocol), VNC (Virtual Network
 Computing), and SSH (Secure Shell / Open SSH).
 External plugins are also supported to add new protocols and features.

The player's goal is to have one of each type of species escape to the center of the ship. A group of unique individuals, one for each species, will give the player the strength they need to overpower the alien guards and release everyone.

firefox-addons:2998424.name: AdBlock — Ads, Trackers
firefox-addons:2998424.summary: Block ads, trackers, and known malicious domains with simple site controls and focus tools.Block ads, trackers, and known malicious domains with simple site controls and focus tools.
firefox-addons:2998424.description:
AdBlock — Ads, Trackers & Site Control helps make browsing cleaner and less distracting by blocking known advertising and tracking requests directly in your browser.
Core features
• Block common advertising and tracking requests using built-in filtering rules
• Block requests to known malicious or unsafe domains
• Pause protection on the current site
• Allowlist trusted websites
• Focus mode for selected distracting sites
• Manage custom blocking rules from the dashboard
• Store all settings locally in the browser
Permissions explanation:
• declarativeNetRequest: used to block network requests matching filter rules
• storage: used to save user settings
• alarms: used to update rules periodically
• host permissions: required to apply filtering across websites
How it works
The extension uses browser-supported request filtering to block unwanted network requests before they load.
Some optional cosmetic filtering may be applied on supported sites to reduce visible clutter.
What this extension does
• Reduces unwanted requests and improves page loading experience
• Provides per-site control (pause and allowlist)
• Helps users stay focused with simple site controls
• Keeps all settings stored locally on the user’s device
What this extension does not do
• Does not collect, store, or transmit personal browsing data
• Does not require an account or sign-in
• Does not use remote code execution
• Does not guarantee blocking of all ads or trackers on every website
Privacy
This extension does not collect or transmit user data.
All blocking and filtering are performed locally within the browser.

firefox-addons:994977.summary:
aka R20ES provides quality-of-life and workflow speed improvements to the Roll20 VTT.

firefox-addons:994977.description:

And many other misc. features!

apple-macos:6818143047.description:
Flash Books gathers your HTML, PDF, ePub, documents, slides, images and more on one bookshelf and lets you read them like printed books. Even HTML documents become books you can page through.
■ Formats
- HTML, Markdown, plain text, RTF and web archives
- PDF, ePub and CBZ (image archives such as comics)
- Documents (.doc, .docx), spreadsheets (.xls, .xlsx) and presentations (.ppt, .pptx), shown as pages and slides
- Pages, Numbers and Keynote documents saved as a single file
- Images (JPEG, PNG, HEIC, TIFF, GIF, WebP and more)
- Add books from Files, open them in Flash Books from another app, add several at once from the share sheet, or use the Add Books shortcut
■ Bookshelf
- Switch between a cover grid and a list with titles and authors. Covers show a book's thickness by its page count.
- Organize books in collections. A book can belong to several collections.
- Label books with colored tags to search, filter and group them. Flag books and show only the flagged ones.
- Stack books together, and archive the ones you have finished.
- Sort manually, by title reading, recently opened, newest first, oldest first or by tag.
- Search by title, author and tag.
■ Reading
- Read in two-page spreads in landscape, or in single pages, with the cover on its own page if you like.
- Left-to-right, right-to-left and vertical page order.
- Turn pages with a page curl, a slide, a slide over, a crossfade or instantly.
- The pages you have read and the pages left show as paper edges beside the page.
- For ePub, HTML and other text, change the font and text size. PDF and others can scroll as well as page.
- Documents (.doc, .docx) can also scroll continuously, keeping only explicit page breaks.
- Select and copy text. On supported devices, text in images and scanned pages can be selected too.
- Jump with the table of contents, page thumbnails and bookmarks.
- Slide along the overview strip to reach any page in the book.
- Turn pages with a keyboard or a game controller.
- On iPhone Duo, read full screen on the closed display or the large open display.
■ iCloud sync (only when you turn it on)
- Sync book details, original files, covers, collections, tags, bookmarks and reading positions between your iPhone, iPad and Mac through your own iCloud.
- Books from your other devices show their covers, and download when you open them, or all at once with Download All.
- On a cellular connection, the app asks before downloading a large original.
- Short on space? Remove a book's download and keep the original in iCloud.
■ Your data
- No account needed. The app does not collect data.
- Network access from inside books is off by default. You can allow it for a book while you read it.
- Imported source files are never changed.

gnome-extensions:accent-hold@griffit.gma.name: Accent Hold
gnome-extensions:accent-hold@griffit.gma.summary:
Hold a letter (e, a, c, o, n…) and pick its accented variant (é è ê ë, ç, ñ, ô…) from a popup, with its number, the arrows or the mouse; a quick tap types the letter as usual. Works on any keyboard layout, without a daemon or root, in applications that use the GNOME input method (Wayland: GTK, VTE terminals, Electron with its Wayland backend). A shortcut (Super+E by default) opens the same picker without holding, and also works in the other applications (XWayland, Qt 5): there the chosen character is pasted through the clipboard, whose previous content is put back right after.
How a variant is picked is up to you. By default the variants stay open after you let go of the letter and Enter, a number or a click picks one, as on macOS. An option in the preferences makes releasing the letter pick the highlighted variant instead, as in PowerToys Quick Accent.
